headline: Heterogeneous graph networks predict drug-gene, drug-target, and drug synergy outcomes
label: Graph Learning Molecular Interactions
summary: Multi-relational biological graphs are now used for drug-target, synergy, and synthetic lethality prediction, increasingly with interpretability built in.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learning over heterogeneous or multi-relational biological networks to predict pairwise outcomes, including chemical-gene interactions, drug-target affinity, drug synergy, and synthetic lethality. OMNI applies multi-view heterogeneous graph attention with an MLP decoder to a 124,604-node network and reports AUROC 0.91. PMHGT-DTA combines pretrained models with a hierarchical graph transformer over 3D drug graphs and cross-attention, while MGANSL uses a GAN to build multi-network gene-pair representations. A directed weighted network method models effect propagation and attenuation between drug targets and inter-target regulation rather than learning embeddings. What is new here is the pairing of multi-relational structure with explanation: SDCInterpreter couples relational GCN and mask learning with Dijkstra path extraction for synergy prediction, so the explanation is tied to the graph rather than added on top of the architecture.
